 # ADR-0073 — `Foldable`: eager polymorphic reduction over a protocol
 
-**Status:** Accepted (direction) · the **concrete-element** form is implemented and verified on the BEAM; the **element-generic** form is deferred behind **ADR-0074** (associated types). Debated 2026-06-15.
-**Implemented:** partial — `Foldable` + `fsum`/`fany_pos`/`fall_pos`/`fcount` over two container types (`examples/rian/foldable.rian`, `test/rian/prim_test.exs`), running on the BEAM and reach-gated honestly. Element-generic `Foldable(T)` and the lazy-iterator surface are **not** implemented (by design / pending ADR-0074).
+**Status:** Accepted · **ELEMENT-GENERIC** via ADR-0074's associated types — the `Int53` pin is retired. Debated 2026-06-15.
+**Implemented:** yes (eager) — `Foldable` with an associated `type Elem` (ADR-0074): one `fcount` reduces a `Bag` of `Int53` **and** a `Words` of `String` (`examples/rian/foldable.rian`, `test/rian/prim_test.exs`), running on the BEAM, reach-gated honestly (`[:ex, :js]` for the sum-dispatch consumer), and the Rust lowering rustc-verified (ADR-0074 Stage 3). The **lazy-iterator** surface remains deliberately unimplemented (per Decision §2 — laziness is native-per-target, ADR-0057).
 **Refines:** ADR-0047 (portable prelude — Tier 2 over the Tier-1 `List` reducers), ADR-0042 (protocols/impls/bounded generics — the mechanism this rides), ADR-0061 (multi-target protocol lowering — the reach reality below).
 **Refs:** ADR-0057 (concurrency/laziness native-per-target — the *principle* for rejecting lazy iterators), ADR-0034 (no `nil`; totality), ADR-0064 (portable `Int53`), ADR-0035 (no hidden control flow), ADR-0000 (honesty: the matrix matches the emitters).
 **Owners:** Arthur Pendelton (bounds / dispatch) · Maya Lin (emitters) · Elena Rostova (Rust traits / coherence) · Kira Neri (Reach honesty) · Mira (totality) · Rachel Okafor (PM)

A type-system feature that touches the (deliberately conservative) checker, so it is sequenced as the staged plan below, not landed in one drop. -**Implemented:** partial — **Stage 1 (parse + IR) + Stage 2 (coherence) shipped** (`Rian.Decl`, `Rian.Protocol.check_assoc!`; `test/rian/protocol_test.exs`). Parse: a bodiless `type Elem` in a `protocol` → `protocol.assoc = ["Elem"]`; `type Elem := Concrete` in an `impl` → `impl.assoc = %{"Elem" => "Int53"}`. Coherence: an `impl` must bind **exactly** its protocol's declared associated types — missing, bare (`type Elem` with no `:=`), and undeclared bindings all raise `Rian.Protocol.Error` at parse time. **Empirical reframing:** an element-generic `Foldable` (with `Self.Elem`/`C.Elem` projections) already PARSES, type-checks (the checker treats the projection conservatively as `:unknown`), and RUNS on the BEAM (types erase) — so the projection was never a *blocker*; the guarantee that was actually missing was impl-completeness, which Stage 2 now enforces. **Stage 2b (checker resolution) — investigated and DROPPED, not deferred.** The premise was "resolve `C.Elem` to the concrete element so cross-type mismatches are *caught*." But the checker is so conservative it does not flag even a plain return/body mismatch — `def f() Vec(Int53) := 42` type-checks clean (verified). With no mismatch-detection to feed, resolving the projection in the checker would catch *nothing*. Associated-type resolution has exactly one real consumer — the **Rust emitter**, which *must* turn `Vec(Elem)` into `Vec` — so the resolver lives in Stage 3, not the checker. -- [foldable.rian](foldable.rian) — **Tier 2: `Foldable`, eager polymorphic reduction
-  over a protocol (ADR-0073).** A one-method protocol (`to_list(self) Vec(Int53)`)
-  bridges any container to a list, so `fsum`/`fany_pos`/`fall_pos`/`fcount` are written
-  ONCE and dispatch over `Bag` AND `Span` by runtime type (ADR-0042). Eager — no lazy
-  `Iterator` (rejected, ADR-0057). Honest limits: the protocol is single-`Self` (no
-  associated type), so the element is concrete `Int53` today (element-generic deferred);
-  and a sum-dispatch consumer reaches `[:ex, :js]` (the constructor-tag atom pins off
-  `:rs`/`:jvm`) — exactly the reach of the shipped `Show`-over-`Expr`. Verified on BEAM.
+- [foldable.rian](foldable.rian) — **Tier 2: `Foldable`, eager ELEMENT-GENERIC reduction
+  over a protocol (ADR-0073 + ADR-0074).** A one-method protocol with an **associated
+  type** (`type Elem; to_list(self) Vec(Elem)`) bridges any container to a list, so the
+  element is fixed per impl (`type Elem := Int53` / `:= String`) and ONE `fcount` reduces
+  a `Bag` of `Int53` **and** a `Words` of `String` — dispatched by runtime type (ADR-0042).
+  Eager — no lazy `Iterator` (rejected, ADR-0057). Honest reach: a sum-dispatch consumer
+  is `[:ex, :js]` (the constructor-tag atom pins off `:rs`/`:jvm`, exactly the shipped
+  `Show`-over-`Expr`); associated types erase on the BEAM and only the Rust emitter
+  materialises them (`trait { type Elem; }`). Verified on BEAM (+ rustc for the lowering).

 # ===========================================================================
-# `Foldable` — EAGER polymorphic reduction over a protocol (ADR-0073 / ADR-0042)
+# `Foldable` — EAGER polymorphic reduction, ELEMENT-GENERIC (ADR-0074 / ADR-0073)
 # ===========================================================================
-# Tier 1 (`prelude_list.rian`) gave `sum`/`any`/`all`/`length` over a concrete
-# `Vec`. Tier 2 lifts them to ANY container that can produce its elements, via a
-# one-method protocol — the eager, typed analogue of Python's "any iterable":
+# Tier 1 (`prelude_list.rian`) gave `sum`/`any`/`all`/`length` over a concrete `Vec`.
+# Tier 2 lifts them to ANY container via a one-method protocol — the eager, typed
+# analogue of Python's "any iterable". With ADR-0074's **associated type**, the
+# element is no longer pinned to `Int53`: the protocol's `type Elem` is fixed by each
+# impl, so ONE reducer serves containers of DIFFERENT element types.
 #
-#   protocol Foldable { to_list(self) -> Vec(Int53) }
+#   protocol Foldable { type Elem; to_list(self) -> Vec(Elem) }
 #
-# A reducer is then written ONCE against the protocol (`fsum`/`fany`/`fall`) and
-# dispatches to each impl by the receiver's runtime type (ADR-0042 first-arg
-# dispatch). `fsum(Bag([1,2,3]))` and `fsum(Sp(4,5))` call the SAME `fsum`.
+# `fcount` below is element-AGNOSTIC (it counts, not sums), so the SAME `fcount`
+# reduces a `Bag` of `Int53` AND a `Words` of `String` — selected by runtime type
+# (ADR-0042 first-arg dispatch). That is the element-generic win the `Int53`-pinned
+# ADR-0073 draft could not express.
 #
-# DELIBERATELY EAGER. `to_list` materialises — there is no lazy `Iterator`, which
-# would need a portable lazy-sequence abstraction Rian does not provide (laziness
-# is native-per-target, like concurrency in ADR-0057).
-#
-# TWO honest limits of today's protocol mechanism (ADR-0042/0061), both in the ADR:
-#   * No associated/element type — `Self` is one concrete type — so `to_list`
-#     fixes a CONCRETE element (`Int53`) here. An element-generic `Foldable(T)`
-#     needs associated types (deferred).
-#   * Dispatching over SUM types uses a constructor-tag atom in the BEAM/JS
-#     desugaring, so `Rian.Reach` pins these dispatchers to `[:ex, :js]` (exactly
-#     as it does the shipped `Show`-over-`Expr`); primitive-dispatch protocols
-#     (`Eq`/`Ord`) reach all four. Verified on the BEAM.
+# DELIBERATELY EAGER (`to_list` materialises — no lazy `Iterator`, ADR-0057). Honest
+# limits (ADR-0074):
+#   * `type Elem` is resolved per impl; on the BEAM it ERASES (runtime dispatch is
+#     unchanged), and only the Rust emitter materialises it (`trait { type Elem; }` +
+#     `impl { type Elem = i64; }`, ADR-0074 Stage 3).
+#   * dispatching over SUM types uses a constructor-tag atom, so `Rian.Reach` pins
+#     these dispatchers to `[:ex, :js]` (exactly as the shipped `Show`-over-`Expr`);
+#     associated types are erased and do NOT change that. Verified on the BEAM.
 # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 
-# the bridge: a container yields its elements as a concrete list.
+# the bridge: a container yields its elements. `Elem` is the associated element type.
 protocol Foldable do
-  def to_list(self Self) Vec(Int53)
+  type Elem
+  def to_list(self Self) Vec(Elem)
 end
 
+# two containers with DIFFERENT element types — the point of the associated type.
 type Bag := Bag(items Vec(Int53))
-type Span := Sp(lo Int53, hi Int53)
+type Words := Words(items Vec(String))
 
-# impl methods take a plain receiver and destructure with `case` (ADR-0042 — the
-# dispatcher binds the receiver; the head is not a constructor pattern).
 impl Foldable for Bag do
+  type Elem := Int53
   def to_list(b) := case b do Bag(xs) -> xs end
 end
 
-impl Foldable for Span do
-  def to_list(s) := case s do Sp(a, b) -> [a, b] end
+impl Foldable for Words do
+  type Elem := String
+  def to_list(w) := case w do Words(ss) -> ss end
 end
 
-# ── reducers written ONCE over the protocol; `forall T: Foldable` enforces the
-#    bound at every call site (a non-Foldable type is a compile error) ─────────
-def fsum(x T) Int53 forall T: Foldable := sum_l(to_list(x))
-def fany_pos(x T) Bool forall T: Foldable := anypos_l(to_list(x))
-def fall_pos(x T) Bool forall T: Foldable := allpos_l(to_list(x))
-def fcount(x T) Int53 forall T: Foldable := len_l(to_list(x))
-
-# the concrete `Vec(Int53)` folds these bottom out in (cf. `List.*` in
-# prelude_list.rian — inlined here so the example is one self-contained module).
-def sum_l(Vec(Int53)) Int53
-def sum_l([]) := 0
-def sum_l([h | t]) := h + sum_l(t)
-
-def anypos_l(Vec(Int53)) Bool
-def anypos_l([]) := false
-def anypos_l([h | t]) := if h > 0 do true else anypos_l(t) end
-
-def allpos_l(Vec(Int53)) Bool
-def allpos_l([]) := true
-def allpos_l([h | t]) := if h > 0 do allpos_l(t) else false end
+# ── an ELEMENT-AGNOSTIC reducer: one `fcount` over any Foldable, any element type.
+#    `forall C: Foldable` enforces the bound at every call site. ───────────────
+def fcount(x C) Int53 forall C: Foldable := len_l(to_list(x))
 
-def len_l(Vec(Int53)) Int53
+# the concrete fold it bottoms out in — generic over the element (cf. `List.length`
+# in prelude_list.rian; inlined here so the example is one self-contained module).
+def len_l(Vec(T)) Int53 forall T
 def len_l([]) := 0
 def len_l([_ | t]) := 1 + len_l(t)
 
-# fsum(Bag([1,2,3])) = 6 · fsum(Sp(4,5)) = 9 · fall_pos(Sp(-1,2)) = false ·
-# fany_pos(Bag([0,0,3])) = true · fcount(Bag([1,2,3])) = 3 — one reducer set,
-# two container types, selected by runtime shape.
+# fcount(Bag([1,2,3])) = 3 (Int53 elements) · fcount(Words(["a","b"])) = 2 (String
+# elements) — ONE reducer, two element types, dispatched by runtime shape. Numeric
+# reductions (`sum`/`any`/`all`) live in prelude_list.rian over a concrete `Vec`,
+# since they require a specific element type (`Int53`/`Bool`), not any `Elem`.
